items.name: Tottori Sand Dunes
items.kicker: Free, and the reason people first hear of Tottori
items.body:
Japan's largest coastal dune system, and free — no ticket, no gate. From JR Tottori Station's bus terminal it's a ≈20-minute bus to the 鳥取砂丘（砂丘会館）stop, which is how a party with no rental car gets here; there is also a weekend-only Loop Kirin Lion bus at ≈30 minutes, no use on a Tue–Fri trip.

Early morning is still the quietest window, but two independent 2025 firsthand accounts agree it's no longer an undiscovered secret — expect other early visitors too, a shift both attribute to social media popularizing sunrise trips. ⚠ Don't inherit a clock time from a summer account: late October sunrise here is well after 6am, so check the actual time for your date before setting an alarm for eight people.

From the dune overlook, the official city walking route down the camels' own commute path — ≈20 minutes one way to the Horse's Back ridge, ≈40 there and back — is worth-the-detour if the crowd at the entrance feels like the whole point. The camels themselves make that walk to their work stations around 9:15am.

items.name: Sand Museum
items.kicker: Sand sculpture on a scale that has to be seen to make sense
items.body: Next to the dunes. 9:00–18:00, last entry 17:30, ¥800 adult. The 17th exhibition period, themed Spain, runs through Jan 3 2027 — so a late-Oct 2026 visit sees the Spain-themed sculptures.

items.name: Tottori Castle Ruins
items.kicker: Free park; the mansion inside it is not open
items.body: Kyusho Park, the castle-ruins grounds in Tottori city, is free and outdoor. Jinpukaku — the Meiji-era Western mansion generic guides list as the headline stop here — has been closed for preservation work since Dec 29, 2023 (exterior sheeted as of Sep 2025, expected to run several more years). The adjoining Horyu-in garden and Hosen-an teahouse on the same grounds remain open, 9:00–17:00.

items.name: Uradome Coast — San'in Matsushima sightseeing cruise
items.kicker: 40 minutes on the water among the coast's sea stacks
items.body:
San'in Matsushima Yuran's standard cruise runs Mar–Nov, departing hourly 9:30–15:30, ¥1,800 adult, ≈40 min on the water (≈1 hour including boarding). It's weather-dependent — the operator's own site tells visitors to confirm conditions before coming out.

It is not on the four-day plan, and that is a deliberate call rather than an oversight: the last sailing is 15:30, which rules out the arrival afternoon, and Wednesday is already the luggage-and-transfer day. It's the swap if you'd trade the Tottori Castle ruins morning for it.

⚠ Access from Tottori Station couldn't be confirmed from the operator's page — all it publishes is the departure address, 岩美郡岩美町大谷2182, up the coast in Iwami town — so check the connection with the operator (050-5433-9129) before committing a morning to it. This entry deliberately carries no map pin for the same reason: the coordinates it shipped with pointed at the other Matsushima, in Miyagi Prefecture, and no verified pin has replaced them yet.

items.name: Kurayoshi Shirakabe Dozo-gun
items.kicker: White-walled Edo/Meiji warehouses along the Tama River canal
items.body: Free to wander. Reached from stand 2 at Kurayoshi Station's bus terminal by a ≈12-minute city bus to the 赤瓦・白壁土蔵群 stop — every 5–10 minutes outside a few quiet hours, so it's the one leg eight people can take without timing it. The district's own tourist information center, inside Akagawara Building No. 10, is open 9:00–17:00 and runs guided walks at ¥3,300 per guide per hour if the group wants more than a self-guided wander — for eight, that's one guide, not eight tickets.

items.name: Sanbutsu-ji — the Nageiredo climb
items.kicker: Japan's most-cited 'dangerous' National Treasure, on a same-day weather call
items.body:
A wooden hall wedged into a cliff face, reached by a genuine mountain climb with chains and rock scrambles — not a paved path. Reception 8:00–15:00, mandatory 16:30 descent; ¥1,200 adult includes the base temple fee (general temple admission without the climb is ¥400). A minimum of two people is required (no solo climbers), hiking-style footwear is checked at the desk, and entry is refused outright in rain, snow, or any condition the temple judges dangerous — plan it as a same-day decision, not a fixed booking.

The route is typically closed for snow from December through March, so an Oct 20–23 visit is inside the climbing season. Rental straw sandals (waraji) are available at the gate for a fee if your shoes don't pass the footwear check — ⚠ the temple publishes no price for them, so bring cash and ask.

Car-free access is the 70/71 bus from Kurayoshi Station or the Misasa Onsen bus centre to the Mitokusan parking stop — only a handful of runs a day each way, so the bus, not the temple's own hours, is what actually sets your window here. Times are in the Transit tab.

items.name: Nageiredo Yohaijo (viewing platform)
items.kicker: The accessible way to see the same National Treasure
items.body:
A free public viewing platform at the foot of Mitokusan — officially the only place besides climbing where Nageiredo can be seen. It was fitted out in autumn 2022 with Nikon telescopes, which are what make the distance work; the hall is a long way up a cliff from here. It reads in any weather, which is the point on a day the climb itself gets called off.

Reach it on the 70/71 bus to the Mitokusan parking stop — see the Transit tab; the platform's own parking is 2 spaces plus 1 accessible space, with Mitokusan's lots as overflow, so it was never somewhere a party of eight arrives under its own steam. Pair the visit with the Sanbutsu-ji main-hall admission, which also doesn't require the climb.

items.name: Kabuyu
items.body: The public bathhouse marking where Misasa Onsen's radium-spring history began, still called 'motoyu' (the original bath) locally. ¥400 adult; a free footbath and drinking-spring station sit alongside it, open daily except reduced Monday footbath hours.

items.claim: Jinpukaku, the Western-style mansion in the castle ruins park, is a top Tottori city sight.
items.correction: It's been closed for preservation work since Dec 29 2023 and its exterior is currently sheeted for construction — expected to run several more years. The garden and teahouse beside it are still open; the mansion itself isn't.

items.claim: Come to Tottori in October for the crab.
items.correction: Matsuba-gani, the region's marquee crab, is a November–March catch — it is not landed during an Oct 20–23 trip. Beni-zuwaigani (red snow crab) runs September–June and is the one actually in season; ask for it by name.

items.claim: The Nageiredo hike is a must-do photo stop on any Tottori itinerary.
items.correction: It's a real mountain climb — chains, rock scrambles, a 2-person minimum, footwear inspection, and a same-day weather cancellation — not a casual add-on, especially for a group with limited-mobility travelers. The free Nageiredo Yohaijo viewing platform is the honest way for anyone who shouldn't attempt it to still see the hall.

items.claim: Arrive at the Sand Dunes at dawn to have them to yourself.
items.correction: Dawn is still the quietest window, but it isn't empty — two independent 2025 accounts describe other early visitors already there, a shift driven by social media promoting sunrise trips. Expect company, just less of it than midday.
